Section 1

Overview

Purpose

This guide is the standard procedure for deploying the Ikshana website to Cloudflare and connecting a custom domain to it.

Scope

Configuration, data migration, secrets, deployment, domain setup, maintenance and troubleshooting. Changes to site features are out of scope.

Ikshana runs entirely on Cloudflare's free plan as one Worker, live at ikshana.lakshmanasaikarumuri.workers.dev. No Supabase, Render or R2 is involved, and no payment method is needed.

PartCloudflare serviceWhat it holds
Website (React build in dist/)Workers static assetsPages, scripts, styles; refreshes on any route return the app
API (/api/*, /health)Worker running the Express serverLogins, events, gallery, admin tools, registrations
DatabaseD1 ikshana-db (SQLite)Users, events, photos, leadership, settings, registrations
Files (/uploads/*)Workers KV ikshana-mediaImages, event uploads, help-request documents
EmailGmail SMTP from the WorkerPassword-reset and registration emails

Procedures 1–5 (sections 3–7) rebuild the deployment from scratch on any Cloudflare account. Procedure 6 (section 8) connects a custom domain once the site is live. Commands run in D:\ikshana-master-main\main unless a step says otherwise.

2
Section 2

Prerequisites

You need four things before starting; all are free.

  • Node.js 18 or newer (tested with v24) — check with node -v
  • A Cloudflare account on the free plan — sign up at dash.cloudflare.com; no card needed
  • The project folder ikshana-master-main/main with package.json, server.ts, worker.ts and wrangler.jsonc
  • A Gmail account with 2-Step Verification on, for sending emails through an app password
i
Tooling

Wrangler, Cloudflare's command-line tool, is installed with the project (npm install), so there is nothing else to install. Run it as npx wrangler … from the project folder.

3
Section 3 · Procedure 1

Project configuration

These files are already in the project; this step is a checklist, not work. The Express server runs unchanged inside a Worker through Cloudflare's Node.js compatibility, and every Supabase-style query is answered by D1 and KV.

FilePurpose
wrangler.jsoncWorker name, D1 and KV bindings, static assets from dist/, non-secret settings (APP_URL, SMTP_*)
worker.tsEntry point: serves /uploads/* from KV (signed links for private files), passes everything else to Express
cloudflare/expose-env.tsMakes the D1/KV bindings visible to server.ts
server/d1-supabase.tsAdapter: the Supabase query and storage calls the code uses, backed by D1 and KV
migrations/0001_init.sqlD1 schema: 17 tables plus a registration-number counter
cloudflare/vite-stub.jsKeeps the Vite dev server out of the Worker bundle
tools/export-supabase-to-d1.mjs, tools/build-kv-bulk.mjsOne-time copy of data and images from the old Supabase project
.env.productionSecrets file (git-ignored): JWT_SECRET
i
Settings that matter

Two settings in wrangler.jsonc matter if you edit it: compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"] lets Express run, and define pins NODE_ENV to production so local tests match the live site. The original server is kept as server.ts.bak-before-cloudflare.

4
Section 4 · Procedure 2

Account access and resources

This creates the two Cloudflare resources the Worker needs and points wrangler.jsonc at them. It takes about five minutes.

  1. Install the project's packages:

    Commandnpm install

  2. Log in to Cloudflare. A browser tab opens; click Allow. If it warns that a parameter doesn't match, close old login tabs and run it again.

    Commandnpx wrangler login

  3. Create the D1 database, then copy the database_id it prints into d1_databases[0].database_id in wrangler.jsonc:

    Commandnpx wrangler d1 create ikshana-db

  4. Create the KV namespace for files, then copy the id it prints into kv_namespaces[0].id in wrangler.jsonc:

    Commandnpx wrangler kv namespace create ikshana-media
ResourceCurrent ID (not secret)
D1 database ikshana-dbceffffaf-a2be-404d-93ec-f2c77faced4f
KV namespace ikshana-media13a1e454c0084d86a84c5d9e5e42189c
i
Why KV instead of R2

R2 has to be enabled in the Cloudflare dashboard first and may ask for a card. KV needs no activation and covers the site's file storage within the free plan.

5
Section 5 · Procedure 3

Database schema and data migration

The schema step is always needed; the copy steps are only for moving data from the old Supabase project (already done once on 16 November 2026: 163 rows and 126 images).

  1. Create the tables in D1:

    Commandnpx wrangler d1 migrations apply ikshana-db --remote

  2. MIGRATION ONLY Export Supabase data and images into .migration/. With the public (anon) key only public rows are copied; the secret key copies every table. In PowerShell:

    PowerShell$env:SUPABASE_URL="https://cfzrscdvohvupmuiwryb.supabase.co"; $env:SUPABASE_KEY="<supabase key>"; node tools/export-supabase-to-d1.mjs

  3. MIGRATION ONLY Load the rows into D1. The seed clears each table first, so it is safe to re-run:

    Commandnpx wrangler d1 execute ikshana-db --remote --file .migration/seed.sql

  4. MIGRATION ONLY Pack the images and upload them to KV (two batches for about 40 MB):

    Commandsnode tools/build-kv-bulk.mjs
npx wrangler kv bulk put .migration/kv-bulk-1.json --binding MEDIA --remote
npx wrangler kv bulk put .migration/kv-bulk-2.json --binding MEDIA --remote

  5. Delete .migration/ when done.

!
Sensitive data

.migration/ holds user password hashes. It is git-ignored but should not be kept after the import.

Image links are rewritten from Supabase Storage URLs to /uploads/<bucket>/<file>, which the Worker serves from KV.

6
Section 6 · Procedure 4

Secrets and configuration

Only passwords and keys are secrets; everything else lives in vars in wrangler.jsonc. Never put a secret in wrangler.jsonc or commit .env.production.

NameKindValueRequired
JWT_SECRETSECRETLong random string; signs logins and private file linksYes
SMTP_PASSSECRET16-letter Gmail app passwordFor email
RAZORPAY_KEY_ID, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRETSECRETFrom the Razorpay dashboardOnly for paid events
APP_URLVARPublic site address, used in reset linksYes
SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORTVARsmtp.gmail.com, 587For email
SMTP_USER, SMTP_FROMVARThe sending Gmail address, and Ikshana Foundation <that address>For email

  1. Generate a JWT_SECRET and save it in .env.production as JWT_SECRET=<value>:

    Commandnode -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(48).toString('base64url'))"

  2. Create the Gmail app password: turn on 2-Step Verification, then create one at App passwords named "Ikshana". Use only the 16 letters; your normal Gmail password is rejected with error 535.

  3. Save it as a secret (you type it; nothing is shown):

    Commandnpx wrangler secret put SMTP_PASS
!
Impact of changes

Changing the JWT secret logs everyone out. Without SMTP_PASS, the site still works but password-reset and registration emails are not sent; for safety the reset link is never shown on screen in production.

7
Section 7 · Procedure 5

Testing, deployment and verification

A local run uses Cloudflare's real runtime with a local copy of D1 and KV, so problems show up before the live site changes.

  1. OPTIONAL Test locally at http://127.0.0.1:8787. The local database starts empty; run Procedure 3's commands with --local instead of --remote to fill it:

    Commandnpm run build && npx wrangler dev --env-file .env.production

  2. Build and deploy. The first deploy must include the secrets file, because the server refuses to start without JWT_SECRET:

    Commandnpm run deploy -- --secrets-file .env.production

  3. Wrangler prints the live address, for example https://ikshana.<account>.workers.dev. Set APP_URL in wrangler.jsonc to it and deploy once more with npm run deploy.

Post-deployment verification checklist

  • /health shows ok
  • Home, Events, Gallery and Founders & Team load with photos
  • Refreshing a page like /gallery still loads the app
  • Signing in works; admin buttons appear for admin accounts
  • An admin photo upload appears, and deleting it removes the image
  • "Forgot password" delivers an email (after Procedure 4's app password)
  • /uploads/event-uploads/x.pdf returns 403 (private files stay private)
i
Live logs

Watch requests and errors while testing with npx wrangler tail ikshana.

8
Section 8 · Procedure 6

Custom domain connection

Connecting a domain is free on Cloudflare; the only cost is the domain itself (about $10–15 a year for a .com). Cloudflare creates the DNS record and the HTTPS certificate automatically. Examples use ikshana.org; use your own domain.

  1. Get a domain. Already own one (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Hostinger…)? Go to step 2. To buy one at cost: dashboard → Domain Registration → Register Domains. A domain bought there is already on Cloudflare, so skip to step 4.

  2. Add the domain to Cloudflare. Dashboard → Add a domain → enter ikshana.org → choose the Free plan. Check the DNS records it imports; keep any MX records if the domain receives email.

  3. Change the nameservers at your registrar. Replace the existing nameservers with the two Cloudflare shows (like ada.ns.cloudflare.com). Turn off DNSSEC at the registrar first if it is on. Wait for Cloudflare's "your domain is now active" email — usually under an hour, at most 24 hours.

  4. Attach the domain to the Worker. Add a routes entry to wrangler.jsonc, next to "workers_dev":

    wrangler.jsonc"routes": [
  { "pattern": "ikshana.org", "custom_domain": true },
  { "pattern": "www.ikshana.org", "custom_domain": true }
],

    Or in the dashboard: Workers & Pages → ikshana → Settings → Domains & Routes → Add → Custom domain. Remove any existing A/CNAME record for those names first, or adding the domain fails.

  5. Point the site at its new address. In wrangler.jsonc set "APP_URL": "https://ikshana.org" so reset links use the domain, then deploy:

    Commandnpm run deploy

  6. Verify. https://ikshana.org/health shows ok, the padlock shows a valid certificate (it can take up to 15 minutes to issue), and a password-reset email links to the new domain.

i
After the domain is live

The workers.dev address keeps working. To retire it, set "workers_dev": false and deploy. Domain email (like contact@ikshana.org) is separate: Cloudflare Email Routing can forward it to Gmail for free.

9
Section 9

Operations and maintenance

After any code change, one command rebuilds the site and publishes it: npm run deploy. Secrets and data are untouched by a deploy.

TaskHow
Database changeAdd a new file such as migrations/0002_add_column.sql, then run npx wrangler d1 migrations apply ikshana-db --remote before deploying the code that uses it.
Backupnpx wrangler d1 export ikshana-db --remote --output backup.sql. D1 also keeps 7 days of history on the free plan; restore with npx wrangler d1 time-travel restore ikshana-db --timestamp <time>.
Roll back a bad deploynpx wrangler rollback
Change a secretnpx wrangler secret put <NAME>; it applies immediately, no redeploy.

Free-plan limits

The free plan costs nothing; when a daily limit is reached, requests fail until midnight UTC instead of being charged.

ServiceFree limitIkshana today
Worker requests100,000 a day (static pages don't count)Far below
Worker CPU per request10 ms officialLogin checks use 67–144 ms; tolerated so far
D15 GB; 5 million row reads and 100,000 writes a dayAbout 300 rows
KV1 GB; 100,000 reads and 1,000 writes a day; 25 MB per fileAbout 40 MB, 126 files
Gmail SMTPAbout 500 emails a dayResets and registrations only
!
The one paid trigger to watch

If sign-in ever fails with Error 1102, either switch password hashing to PBKDF2 (free, about 20 ms) or move to Workers Paid at $5 a month.

10
Section 10

Troubleshooting

Every error below came up during this deployment; the fix is already in the code unless the row says otherwise.

SymptomCauseFix
Gmail error 535-5.7.8 Username and Password not acceptedNormal Gmail password used, or a mistyped app passwordACTION Create a new 16-letter app password; npx wrangler secret put SMTP_PASS
Login fails with Error 1102Password check used too much CPU for the free planACTION Switch hashing to PBKDF2, or Workers Paid ($5/month)
Deploy refused: supabaseUrl is requiredCloudflare's startup check runs without bindingsFIXED Bindings are looked up per request
Worker crashes: require_streams(...) is not a functionOld iconv-lite used by ExpressFIXED overrides pins iconv-lite 0.6.3 in package.json
API says Http server with port 3000 not found locallywrangler dev set NODE_ENV to developmentFIXED define pins NODE_ENV to production
Local requests hang, even /healthOld workerd processes still runningACTION Stop them: Get-Process workerd | Stop-Process -Force (PowerShell)
Local login returns 500 after adding the database IDLocal D1 is keyed by ID, so it's a new empty copyACTION Re-run Procedure 3 with --local
npx wrangler login warns a parameter doesn't matchAn older login tab answeredACTION Close old Cloudflare login tabs; log in again
npm error ECOMPROMISED Lock compromisedTwo npx commands at onceACTION Use the project's copy: node_modules\.bin\wrangler
Help request with large files failsD1 rows are capped at 2 MBFIXED Attachments go to KV as private files
Custom domain won't attachAn A/CNAME record already exists for that nameACTION Delete that DNS record, then add the domain again
